# YM07: 慈云普护 Ciyun Puhu, "Merciful Clouds Universally Protecting"

Malone calls it Island of Shrines.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM07` · Page: `/scenes/#YM07` · Row: `research/buildings/YM07-ciyun-puhu/`

## What it was

慈云普护 Ciyun Puhu, the shrine island on the north shore of the Back Lake, west of 碧桐书院: a front hall of three bays facing the lake, 欢喜佛场 Huanxi Fochang; north of it a three-bay storeyed building with the plaque 慈云普护, Guanyin above and Guandi below; to the east 龙王殿, the shrine of the Dragon King of the garden, 昭福龙王 (S05 j80:35b-36a). Plaques by Yongzheng (S05 j80:36a). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **changed** Differs on later plans (S41); **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S41, S01).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Lyric of 1744 (to 菩薩蠻): "有樓三層刻漏鐘表在焉殿供觀音大士其傍為道士廬" (S05 j80:36b). A path runs between two lakes under wisteria; there is a three-storey tower holding a water clock and clocks, a hall for Guanyin and beside it a Daoist's lodge, like the stone bridge of Tiantai.

## Interior and setting

### Interior

Nothing written yet.

### The garden around it

On a strip between two waters (一徑界重湖間), with wisteria on trellises and tree-peonies (鼠姑) (S05 j80:36b). The clock tower is the scene's landmark on the album leaf; S01 marks a 钟亭 (YM07-N01).

## Gaps and wishlist

The three-storey tower of the lyric (樓三層刻漏鐘表, S05 j80:36b) is on the leaf P0007 a separate hexagonal red tower with three roofs, standing west of the two-storey 慈云普护 hall: it is the 钟亭 of S01 (YM07-N01), not the three-bay hall. Its size and the clockwork are not described. No dig.
